built.summary:
Both items are fixed in the files I own. backend tsc is clean, and every suite I ran passes: the new tests/integrationPass2Orders.test.ts (15 tests, two companies) plus 25 existing files (orders, kitchen, expo/KDS, till, dispatch, online checkout). resimKitchen also passes with RESIM_K_OTHER=1.

NEEDS 5 (pre-orders, O-RV-3). A pre-order is now "held" when its scheduled time is more than 60 minutes (PRE_ORDER_PREP_MS) after the order was created. The check reads the stored row, so the order-creation path and the release worker always agree.
- **At creation:** order creation (ingestOrder) neither sends order:new to the kitchen screens nor takes stock for a held order. The customer receipt still goes out.
- **Release:** a new worker, workers/preOrderRelease.ts, runs every 60 seconds and goes company by company. It calls releaseDuePreOrders(tenantId), which releases each held order once its time is within 60 minutes: it sends order:new, then takes the stock. Each order is claimed under its row lock by an audit row ('order.pre_order_released', category 'system', stamped with the order's company), so a second tick or a second server does nothing. Cancelled or rejected orders are never released.
- **Firing early:** if expo Fire or fire-course fires a held pre-order before its window, it is released on the spot.
- **Expo queue:** a held pre-order is left out of awaitingFire and inProgress, so a week of pre-orders no longer pushes today's orders past the 50- and 80-row caps. An order already 'preparing' always shows. The queue has a new `upcoming` list (each row carries scheduledFor and kitchenAt).
- **Station screens and KDS:** the expo station queue, the station load counts, KDS /stations, /my-stations and /unrouted all leave out the pending lines of a held pre-order.
- **Pacing worker:** it never cooks a pre-order before its window, even if staff confirmed it early.
- **Rider dispatch:** the 6-hour window now uses the later of placedAt and scheduledFor, and an order scheduled more than 60 minutes ahead is never offered. Orders are offered oldest-time first.
- **Storefront:** is_pre_order and scheduled_for are now set only when the time is really in the future. A past time is stored as an order for now.

NEEDS 16 (course pacing, K-RV-01/02).
- **First course:** fireCourse now fires only the lines that are due and returns the rest as `paced`. If nothing of the course has started, it re-sets the schedule first. Later courses still fire whole.
- **Unfired order:** firing the first course of an order still in 'received' is refused with 409 FIRE_FROM_EXPO, so the dish can't be cooking while the order still reads 'received'. It must go through expo's Confirm & Fire.
- **The route:** POST /orders/:id/fire-course takes `fireAll`, allowed only for managers and the expediter (otherwise 403 FIRE_ALL_NOT_ALLOWED). It is audited as 'expo.fire_all' with the order's company. When dishes are paced but nothing fired, it now returns 200 with `paced` instead of 404.
- **K-RV-02 (paid after the schedule expired):** to fix this I also edited processCoursePacingTick, a function outside my listed scope. For a completed till sale or a pre-order whose first course has not started, it re-sets the schedule before firing, so only the longest dish starts. I limited it to those two cases because an order confirmed through the normal route already had its schedule re-set at confirm; this keeps the existing auditOrdersFollowup R7 and auditOrdersKitchen BOH-16 tests passing.

items.note: Pre-orders held until scheduledFor minus 60 min. New worker workers/preOrderRelease.ts (per company, idempotent) sends order:new and takes the stock at that point. Held orders are left out of: the expo awaitingFire and inProgress lists (new `upcoming` list), station queues and loads, KDS /unrouted, the pacing worker and rider dispatch (window uses the later of placedAt and scheduledFor). Expo Fire or fire-course on a held order releases it at once. The storefront sets is_pre_order and scheduled_for only for a future time. Admin and tablet screens don't show `upcoming` yet (see needsOtherFiles).

fireCourse paces the first course: only due lines fire, the rest come back as `paced`, and the schedule is re-set if nothing of the course has started. The route accepts fireAll for managers and the expediter only (403 FIRE_ALL_NOT_ALLOWED), audited as expo.fire_all with the order's company. The first course of an order still in 'received' gets 409 FIRE_FROM_EXPO. When only paced lines remain it returns 200 with `paced`. K-RV-02: the pacing worker re-sets the schedule before firing for a completed till sale or a pre-order whose first course has not started. That change is in processCoursePacingTick, outside my listed scope (see the note in the summary).

built.prodNotes:
- No schema change and no migration. The new worker (startPreOrderReleaseWorker) runs with ENABLE_WORKERS, uses a plain interval (no Redis) and is safe across several servers.
- **Pre-orders already in the database on deploy:**
  - Those already within 60 minutes of their time get one extra order:new on the first tick.
  - Those further out were deducted under the old code and get order:new again when their window opens.
  - Stock is not taken twice in either case: the stock deduction skips any order that already has a 'stock.sale_deplete' row.
- **Behaviour changes:**
  - Pre-orders more than 60 minutes out disappear from expo's awaiting-fire and in-progress lists and from station screens until 60 minutes before their time. The API lists them under `upcoming`, but the admin and tablet screens don't show it yet.
  - Delivery pre-orders are offered to riders only from 60 minutes before their time.
  - POST /orders/:id/fire-course on course 1 now fires only the due dishes. On an order expo has not fired yet it answers 409 FIRE_FROM_EXPO; the admin Courses page button for course 1 on a 'received' order will now fail until item 3 lands.
  - "Fire all now" through fire-course is limited to managers and the expediter, and audited.
- **Pacing worker:** a till sale paid after its pacing schedule expired now starts only its longest dish; the others follow at their gaps, up to about 30 seconds late because the worker ticks every 30 seconds.
built.ownerQuestions:
1. The kitchen and rider lead time for pre-orders is one fixed 60 minutes. Is that right, and should it be per brand? For delivery, offering a rider 60 minutes ahead may leave them idle; a shorter rider lead (for example 20 minutes) is a one-line change.
2. Should course 1 only ever be fired from expo? I made fire-course refuse the first course while the order is still 'received' (409 FIRE_FROM_EXPO), and keep it for paced or already-fired first courses and for later courses. Alternatively, fire-course could be removed for course 1 entirely.
3. Should a pre-order that staff confirm early start cooking at the 60-minute window? That is what happens now, through the pacing worker. Or should it wait for expo to fire it?

review.title: A held pre-order completed before its window, then refunded, never has its stock taken, although COGS is booked
review.scenario: Reproduced on servd_test_ip2_o_rv. A storefront pre-order is placed for 3 h ahead, so it is held and no stock is taken. The customer comes early and staff move it received→confirmed→ready→completed with PATCH /orders/:id/status (admin orders page). None of these steps calls releasePreOrder. Only expo Fire and fire-course do. completeOrder posts the sale entry with COGS (Dr food cost / Cr 1210 Inventory, 220 in the probe), but there is no stock.sale_deplete row and Beef stays at 100. The order is then refunded before scheduledFor−60min. releaseDuePreOrders' SQL excludes 'refunded' (`o.status::text NOT IN ('cancelled','rejected','refunded')`), so it never releases the order: released=false, depleted=0, Beef still 100. The ledger has derecognised inventory that the shelf count still holds, and this never corrects. CLAUDE.md says a refund keeps the depletion because the food was made. Without a refund, stock is still only taken at the window, so it lags COGS by up to 7 days and the auto-86 runs late.
review.fix: 1) In releaseDuePreOrders, stop excluding 'refunded'. Exclude only cancelled/rejected, which matches deductInventoryForOrder's NO_SALE. 2) Release a held pre-order (claim the PRE_ORDER_RELEASE marker and deduct its stock) when it leaves 'received' through transitionOrder, or at the latest in completeOrder. Then every completion has its stock out before or with its COGS. Add a test: complete a held pre-order via updateOrderStatus, set it to refunded, and assert one stock.sale_deplete row.

review.title: A held pre-order finished early through the status buttons is sent to the kitchen again at its window
review.scenario: Reproduced. A pre-order is placed 3 h ahead and staff take it confirmed→ready→completed on the admin orders page. At confirm, transitionOrder lays the pacing schedule (Classic now, Fries +5 min), but its lines stay 'pending' and hidden from every station screen because of kitchenDueWhere. So the kitchen could not have cooked it through the system, and the order was handed over anyway. When time reaches scheduledFor−60min: (a) releaseDuePreOrders still releases it, because 'completed' is not excluded, and sends order:new (KDS haptic/sound) for an order that is already finished; (b) processCoursePacingTick picks it up, because PACING_FIRED includes 'completed' and kitchenDueWhere now passes. The new K-RV-02 re-anchor (`o.status === 'completed' && !started`) re-anchors it and fires Classic onto the grill. In the probe, Classic went to 'preparing' with firedAt set about 2 h after the order was completed. Before this change the dish was fired right after confirm, while the order was live.
review.fix: Limit the pacing worker's 'completed' handling (both the firing and the new re-anchor) to till sales (isTillSale: pos / group bill), which is what UI-05/K-RV-02 are about. Do not release, emit order:new for, or fire a non-till order that is already completed. Better still, apply the OK2-RV-1 fix (release on leaving 'received'), and on 'ready'/'completed' clear scheduledFireAt on the order's pending lines.

review.title: The admin Courses page shows a 'Fire course' button the API now refuses for course 1 of a 'received' order, and errors fail silently
review.scenario: fireCourse now answers 409 FIRE_FROM_EXPO for the first course while the order is 'received'. The Courses page (the only caller of POST /orders/:id/fire-course) still shows 'Fire course →' on every course with `!g.fired`, including course 1 of an unfired order. Its useMutation has no onError, so the tap does nothing and shows no message. It also ignores the new 200 `paced` response: for course 1 after expo Fire it reports success while the shorter dishes stay pending, and the button disappears because `fired` (anyFired) becomes true. The builder listed this under needsOtherFiles but did not change it. The behaviour change reaches users as soon as the backend deploys.
review.fix: In courses/page.tsx, hide the course-1 button while the order is 'received' (or show the 409 message 'fire it from expo'). Add an onError that shows error.message. Show the returned `paced` lines ('Fries fires at HH:MM'). Optionally add 'Fire all now' (`fireAll: true`) for MANAGERS + expediter. This file is outside the backend stream and needs a frontend owner.

review.title: Pre-orders more than 60 minutes out disappear from every kitchen screen, because no screen shows `upcoming`
review.scenario: GET /expo/queue now leaves held pre-orders out of awaitingFire/inProgress and lists them only under `upcoming`. The tablet KDS overview (tablet/app/(staff)/kds/index.tsx builds lanes from awaitingFire/inProgress/ready only) and the admin expo page never read `upcoming`. Station queues also hide their pending lines. A large catering pre-order placed days ahead is therefore invisible to the kitchen until 60 minutes before its time, so there is no time for prep or stock checks. At deploy, every existing future pre-order (including ones already acknowledged) also vanishes from expo and the stations until its window.
review.fix: Render `upcoming` on the admin expo page and the tablet KDS/expo screen ('Pre-order for HH:MM — reaches the kitchen at HH:MM', no Fire button except an explicit early fire for managers). Ship this in the same deploy as the backend change (needsOtherFiles #2).

review.title: The FIRE_FROM_EXPO guard covers only course 1: fire-course still fires a later course of a 'received' (or held) order
review.scenario: fireCourse throws FIRE_FROM_EXPO only when `isFirst && order.status === 'received'`. POST /orders/:id/fire-course {course: 2} on a 'received' order passes this check, releases a held pre-order (releasePreOrder 'fire_course': order:new plus stock), and fires the whole of course 2 through fireOrderItems. Mains then cook before the starters were fired, and the order still reads 'received'. This is the state the new 409 is meant to prevent. Any staff role can do it.
review.fix: Refuse any course while the order is 'received' (or any course above the first open course until that course has started): 409 FIRE_FROM_EXPO.

review.title: A released pre-order placed more than 12 h before its time never shows on KDS /unrouted
review.scenario: /kds/unrouted keeps `order.placedAt >= now − 12h` and now also requires the pending line's order to be kitchen-due (scheduledFor ≤ now+60min). Take a pre-order placed Monday for Wednesday with an unrouted line (no station, or a retired station). Its line is hidden until Wednesday's window, and by then placedAt is more than 12 h old, so it never appears on the list whose purpose is to let the kitchen bump unrouted lines. Before this change it was at least listed for 12 h after it was placed.
review.fix: Key the 12 h window on the effective time, greatest(placedAt, scheduledFor) (`OR: [{placedAt: {gte}}, {scheduledFor: {gte}}]`, the same as riderDispatch now does).

fix.summary:
I checked all six findings and all six are real. I fixed the four backend ones (RV-1, RV-2, RV-5, RV-6) with tests. RV-3 and RV-4 are frontend changes, so they are listed under needsOtherFiles.

**What a held pre-order now does.** Acknowledging it ('confirmed') still keeps it held. If it moves on before its window, it is released:
- at 'preparing', in transitionOrder: stock is taken and the kitchen gets order:new;
- at 'ready' or 'refunded', in transitionOrder: stock is taken, but no order:new;
- at completion: completeOrder releases it before its claim transaction, so the stock always comes out before or with the COGS.

releasePreOrder now:
- skips only cancelled and rejected orders, so a refunded order is still released;
- sends order:new only while the order is received, confirmed or preparing;
- records `status` in the PRE_ORDER_RELEASE metadata;
- does a cheap check outside the lock first, so an order that was never held costs no row lock.

releaseDuePreOrders' SQL no longer excludes 'refunded'.

**Pacing worker (processCoursePacingTick):**
- It no longer fires a non-till order that is 'completed', or one that is 'ready' with nothing of its first course started. It clears those lines' stale fire times instead.
- Re-anchoring now happens only for a paid till sale whose first course has not started, or for a pre-order that is confirmed or preparing.
- It now also picks up an order that already has a fired line. Without this, the shorter dishes of a pre-order fired early at expo would wait until the window, possibly days later. The reviewers did not report this; I found it while fixing RV-2.

**fireCourse (RV-5):** it now refuses any course while the order is 'received' (409 FIRE_FROM_EXPO), not just course 1. I kept the order-level rule and did not add the 'first open course must have started' rule. Expo firing course 2 first on an order that is already fired is still allowed on purpose.

**KDS /unrouted (RV-6):** the 12 h window now uses the effective time, greatest(placedAt, scheduledFor), written as an OR in an AND clause, the same rule rider dispatch uses.

**Scope note:** to fix RV-1 I added two small hooks outside my narrow region of service.ts: one block after the pacing block in transitionOrder and one call at the top of completeOrder. Both call the idempotent releasePreOrder. The other edits are in the pre-order block and the pacing worker, which this stream built. In orders/routes.ts I changed only the fire-course comment.

I did not edit expo/routes.ts, riderDispatch.ts, preOrderRelease.ts, storefront/routes.ts or index.ts.

items.note: Confirmed. A held pre-order is now released when it moves to preparing (with order:new), to ready or refunded (stock only), and in completeOrder before the COGS claim. Releasing on 'confirmed' was left out on purpose: acknowledging a pre-order keeps it held. releaseDuePreOrders and releasePreOrder no longer skip refunded orders. Tests: done early through updateOrderStatus then refunded gives exactly one depletion and the worker does not take it again; completion alone releases it, with the depletion recorded no later than the completion claim; an order refunded before this fix is released by the worker at its window, and company B's pass never touches it.

Confirmed. The release at ready/completion writes the marker, so the window sends no second order:new. The pacing worker no longer fires a non-till 'completed' order, or a 'ready' order with nothing started, and clears their stale fire times. Re-anchoring is limited to paid till sales (K-RV-02) and pre-orders that are confirmed or preparing. Tests: a pre-order done early stays unfired with fire times cleared at its window; a non-till order marked ready is not fired. The K-RV-02 till test still passes.
Real, but it is frontend (frontend/admin/src/app/orders/[id]/courses/page.tsx), outside my files. See needsOtherFiles. With RV-5, the 409 now applies to every course of a 'received' order.
Real, but it is frontend (admin expo page and tablet KDS/expo), outside my files. The backend already returns `upcoming`. See needsOtherFiles.

Confirmed. fireCourse now refuses ANY course while the order is 'received' (409 FIRE_FROM_EXPO). It checks this before any release, so nothing is released or fired. Test: course 2 of a held, received pre-order gives 409 with no release and no depletion, and company B gets 404.

Confirmed. /kds/unrouted's 12 h window is now OR(placedAt >= now−12h, scheduledFor >= now−12h), so the order's effective time is used. Test: a pre-order placed 2 days ago with an unrouted line shows once its window opens. One due in 20 h is still hidden, and company B never sees it.

Whoever owns those functions should keep them when merging.
fix.ownerQuestions: Should acknowledging a pre-order ('confirmed') take its stock right away? I chose no: it stays held until its window or until it goes to preparing, ready or completed. Taking the stock on acknowledgement would keep the shelf count closest to the order book, but it would drain today's stock and auto-86 for orders days ahead, which is what O-RV-3 set out to stop.
fix.prodNotes: Nothing extra at deploy and no migration. Pre-orders completed before this release and still before their window are released by the worker at their window: stock is taken, with no order:new because they are completed or refunded. Those refunded before this release are now released at their window too, provided it is no more than 24 h in the past.
